reply.image_seen: Image 1 shows the patched pump on checkerboard; image 2 isolates its motor, riser, rope and horizontal manifold with narrow end flanges; image 3 places it beside a human; image 4 shows a smaller red sibling; image 5 composites R1 onto ground without runtime attachments; image 6 shows the previous art with open manifold bores, a southern brass attachment and a separate hose.

concerns.evidence: The R1 texture shows wooden supports beneath the manifold centre, with no descending brass attachment. However, the card explicitly assigns couplers to runtime drawing. Image 6 shows a southern attachment on the previous version; no assembled R1 capture establishes whether its runtime stub and coupler appear correctly.

In image 3 the pump has a substantial silhouette beside the human: the manifold spans broadly across the machine and the riser extends north above its body. It neither overflows badly nor floats tiny inside its canvas. Unoccupied space around this irregular silhouette does not establish a footprint failure; the promised footprint outline is also absent.

Image 5 explicitly omits runtime hoses and couplers. Image 6 depicts the replaced picture and does not show a completed connection to a neighbour. Neither establishes that R1's three code-defined ports meet their attachments at the correct positions and planes.
R1's offline composite contains no attached runtime hose, coupler or cord whose overlap can be checked. The previous-art capture cannot verify R1's assembled draw order.

The card specifies Graphic_Single with one picture for every rotation. Images 1, 2, 3 and 5 consistently show that same motor-right, riser-left arrangement and palette. Separate rotated sprite drawings are therefore not required; runtime attachment behaviour across rotations remains unresolved under K3 and K4.

Seen from the building camera, looking down at about 35 degrees: the lit top faces of the borrowed electric motor, the pump casing and the manifold pipe are visible above their front faces. The stub ends in a round bolted flange with a bare, open, dark-bored face, the mounting point where a brass hose coupler attaches. The stub is the same weathered steel as the manifold, with matching bolt heads and a clean dark outline. One picture serves every rotation.

observed.facings.png: Enlarged view of the Scrapper candidate: a round disc with a thick dark brown-black outer ring and a flat, matte taupe-brown inner face. A thin black crescent sits on the right inner rim, where the inner face meets the ring. No hole, no inner tube walls and no depth gradient. The surroundings are transparent.
observed.south.png: The same Scrapper disc at its native 64 px: a dark ring around a flat brown-grey fill, cleanly cut out on transparency.
observed.scale.png: In-game crop of three reels (red Modern at top, black Industrial in the middle, rusty Scrapper at the bottom), each with its laid hose. A right column shows each hose's free tip lying flat and pointing east. These tips show the CURRENT art, an open dark bore hole at the end. A vanilla human stands at the bottom right for scale.
observed.variants_1.png: Industrial candidate: an almost all-black disc with a slightly lighter black ring and a dark charcoal fill, no visible hole.
observed.variants_2.png: Modern candidate: a light grey/beige outer ring with a thin dark outline and a darker grey flat fill. It reads like a closed cap or end face.
observed.variants_3.png: Futuristic candidate: a light grey ring with cyan glowing arc accents at the four quadrants and a dark grey, finely textured fill. No hole.
observed.assembled_1.png: Same crop as the scale image with the candidates pasted over the game's Mouth. Top (Modern): the tip now ends in a narrow upright pale ellipse with a grey rim, a closed end face matching the canvas hose and coupler. Middle (Industrial): the corrugated black hose ends in a dark narrow ellipse that blends into the hose with no hole showing. Bottom (Scrapper): the wrapped hose ends in a thin pale rim ellipse with a dark fill. On every tip the piece sits at the hose's end, squashed edge-on, and follows the hose's angle.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same crop unmodified. Every tip shows a black open bore hole (round on Industrial and Scrapper, oval on Modern), as if the hose's end were turned toward the viewer.

CAMERA.seen: The hose lies flat and points east, so its cut face is nearly edge-on to the 35-degree camera. With the C#'s 0.30 x 0.86 squash, each candidate reads as a narrow upright ellipse at the tip, consistent with that camera.

BORE.seen: All four candidates close the bore with a flat fill and keep only a thin rim crescent. In assembled_1 no tip shows a dark open hole facing the viewer, unlike assembled_2. The hose does not turn toward the camera, so no bore should show, and none does.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1 each pasted piece sits exactly on the hose end at the same height, plane and angle as the hose (placement is set by C#, and the template-matched paste lines up).

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: The only code port is the free end. Each tip has a drawn end face/rim at that point, and no other connectors are drawn. The rim ring still marks it as a cut end, though with the fill closed it reads more like a capped end than an open one (see finding).

LAYERS.seen: The Mouth piece draws over the wrap and hose end on all three tips, with nothing wrongly occluding it.

ROTATIONS.seen: There is a single texture with no facings; C# rotates it along the hose. Across the variants, each look's palette matches its own hose (black for Industrial, light grey for Modern, cyan accents for Futuristic, brown for Scrapper).

SIGNATURE.seen: Each piece reads as the hose's rimmed end face, and the rim ring is recognisable. The fill is flat, so the end reads as closed/solid rather than hollow; that is a polish point, not an identity failure.

MATERIAL.seen: The rims read as rubber or metal and the fills as the cut-end colour of each hose's material. Nothing looks like a flat coat of paint at in-game size.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The disc fills the 64x64 canvas (measured alpha height 62 px) without cropping. Its in-game size is set by C#.

ALPHA.seen: The corners are clean and transparent, with no halo, backdrop or shadow (real alpha present per the measurement).

OURS.seen: Derived from each look's own Mouth piece. No donor art.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell the tip reads as the hose's end. The closed fill removes the black dot, but the rim ring still separates the end from the hose body, most weakly on Industrial, where black blends into black.
